newsitem.title: FRANCE: Part of French Grande Arche faces fire risk closure.
newsitem.headline: Part of French Grande Arche faces fire risk closure.

text.p: Part of the futuristic Grande Arche office block near Paris, one of France's modern architectural monuments, has been threatened with closure because of fire risks, French media said on Friday.
A local court in Nanterre decreed closure of the northern side of the 36-storey arch at La Defense west of the city after an inspection revealed safety risks, France Info public radio said.

It said safety inspectors had found that work ordered to improve fire precautions in the building, where about 2,000 people normally work, had not been carried out. Inspectors would examine the building again on Monday.

A security guard at the arch contacted on Friday night said he was unaware of any closure order. France's TF1 said the building was threatened with closure by the ruling court ruling but had yet to be ordered out.
The spectacular white arch of concrete and glass, by Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen, opened in 1989 when it hosted a summit of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.
The arch, a huge sugar cube with a hole in the middle, was part of a vast remodelling around the capital by late president Francois Mitterrand during his rule from 1981-95.

Some other modern monuments dotting Paris are showing premature signs of age. Nets were hung on the facade of the Bastille Opera last summer because of falling masonry. The arch has also had problems with cracking marble on its facade.
And France is spending $85 million on a millennium facelift for the brightly painted Beaubourg arts centre, which has been worn out by hordes of visitors after just 20 years.
